chunks:
Public oversight of election administration routinely collides with an unnecessary architectural binary: either upload sensitive state voter-history files containing names, birth years, and street addresses to a centralized cloud server, or settle for shallow state press releases without county verification. Running SQL locally inside WebAssembly eliminates that trade-off. When state registration records stay strictly inside browser memory and publish outward only as five-digit `county_fips` aggregates, analysts can join local audits against federal domain tables with zero personal data ever crossing a network boundary.

The institutional justification for this separation is explicit in federal survey design. As the Election Assistance Commission documents in its statutory survey overview:

> "The Election Administration and Voting Survey (EAVS) collects jurisdiction-level data on voter registration, list maintenance, mail ballots, provisional ballots, and polling operations across every U.S. state and territory without collecting personally identifiable voter records."

Building on this aggregate-first boundary inside [local-first](/explore/local-first) browser software allows independent researchers to evaluate list maintenance performance at the county scale. In the Feb 2026 V2.0 EAVS release alone, 6,461 reporting jurisdictions fold cleanly into 3,127 five-digit county FIPS units once New England and Wisconsin municipal rows are aggregated up to their parent counties. Joined against the 2020-2024 Census Citizen Voting Age Population (CVAP) special tabulation and Census county population estimates, the resulting national baseline covers 240,833,718 estimated citizen adults, 226,420,603 total registered voters, 203,680,591 active registrations, and 154,277,745 certified 2024 presidential ballots.

## Why Five-Digit FIPS Joins Beat Raw File Redistribution

Publishing unredacted state voter rolls on public web hosts creates severe [privacy](/explore/privacy) risks even when statutes permit commercial acquisition. Scrapers harvest residential histories, birth dates, and party affiliations to train phishing lures and identity-theft models. A strict aggregate pipeline stops that leakage by enforcing hard schema gates before any JSON or CSV leaves local compute: names, dates of birth, registration IDs, and residential street strings never leave the client's local OPFS or in-memory DuckDB-Wasm table.

When those same state files are distilled down to county-level metrics—such as active registrations, inactive counts, same-ZIP duplicates, out-of-state mailing addresses, and large precincts—they become directly comparable across state lines. In Mississippi (82 counties) and North Carolina (100 counties), matching 2026 state voter-roll metrics against EAVS V2.0 and Census benchmarks immediately surfaces structural contrasts: 1. **List Maintenance Cadence:** During the 2024 reporting cycle, North Carolina sent 707,618 confirmation notices (`A10a`) and processed 971,554 voter removals (`A12a`) against 7,898,142 estimated citizen adults, whereas Mississippi sent 100,185 notices and removed 148,200 registrations against 2,221,778 citizen adults. 2.

**Registration-to-CVAP Alignment:** In 2026 state totals, North Carolina carries 6,902,431 active voters (and 7,900,954 total registered), with only one county—rapidly growing Brunswick County at 136,822 active voters vs. 128,976 ± 410 CVAP (106.08%, alongside +33,821 net domestic migration from 2020 to 2024)—exceeding its upper 90% CVAP margin of error. Mississippi carries 1,882,342 active voters across 82 counties yet records seven counties above the 90% CVAP upper bound, including Humphreys County at 116.01% (6,404 active vs. 5,520 ± 23 CVAP) and Yazoo County at 101.88% despite net domestic out-migration of -3,507 residents.

## Addressing the Honest Counterargument Against Aggregate Tables

Critics of pure aggregate publishing rightly point out that county totals alone cannot confirm whether two identical-looking registration records belong to the same individual or twin siblings sharing a household. Household deduplication and address-change verification happen inside the individual record layer—a computation that genuine [election integrity](/explore/election-integrity) work still requires.

That critique underscores why local-compute DuckDB-Wasm architecture matters. Individual-level matching occurs deterministically inside the analyst's own browser RAM over user-supplied files that never upload to a server. Only the statistical counts per county—high-density 8+ voter addresses, same-ZIP candidate pairs, active-to-CVAP ratios, and provisional rejection rates—graduate into shareable civic benchmarks. Citizens retain mathematical auditability without turning neighbors' street addresses into permanent public downloads.

## Inspecting County Joins Without Server Trust

Replicating this architecture requires neither cloud warehouses nor proprietary dashboards. An analyst can pair any public state export with Census and EAC tables directly through [civic data benchmarks](/explore/civic-data-benchmarks): download official federal CSV distributions, normalize EAVS sentinel negatives (`-99`, `-88`, `-77`) to null rather than zero, aggregate sub-county New England and Wisconsin municipalities into five-digit FIPS rows, and verify SHA-256 digests locally. The reward is a permanent, inspectable civic record where every claim traces back to a primary public URL and zero personal privacy is compromised.

---
**Sources:** [U.S. EAC 2024 EAVS V2.0 CSV Release](https://www.eac.gov/sites/default/files/2026-02/2024_EAVS_for_Public_Release_nolabel_V2_csv.zip) · [U.S. Census Bureau 2020-2024 CVAP Special Tabulation](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial/rdo/datasets/2024/2024-cvap/CVAP_2020-2024_ACS_csv_files.zip) · [U.S. DOJ NVRA Section 8 Guidance](https://www.justice.gov/crt/national-voter-registration-act-1993-nvra)

Civic analytics pipelines collapse quickly when built on brittle web scrapers, undocumented API keys, or noisy volunteer mirrors with mismatched county boundaries. Before adding external tables to a browser-side analytics engine, every upstream repository should survive an automated engineering triage: verify HTTP availability without proprietary tokens, validate stable five-digit county FIPS joins, inspect sentinel missing-value conventions, and enforce zero personally identifiable fields.

Engineering federal open-data feeds for browser execution requires honoring explicit public API schemas rather than assuming uniform CSV dialects. As FEMA's OpenFEMA technical specification explains:

> "OpenFEMA API v2 endpoints return paginated JSON records free of authentication keys so researchers and emergency planners can filter disaster declarations deterministically by county FIPS codes."

Across our repository evaluation for [databases](/explore/databases) and civic analytics, five keyless public sources passed full reproducibility checks and now ship with pinned SHA-256 digests: 1. **U.S. EAC 2024 EAVS V2.0 (Feb 2026 CSV ZIP):** Supplies active/inactive rolls, `A10a` confirmation notices (35,328,942 matched across 50 states + DC; 38,803,086 raw national), `A12a` removals (20,021,606 matched), mail ballot undeliverables (915,949 of 66,149,059 transmitted), and provisional ballots (1,690,565 cast; 422,940 rejected). 2. **Census 2020-2024 ACS CVAP & County Population Estimates:** Provides citizen voting-age denominators (240,833,718 national) with 90% margins of error plus cumulative 2020-2024 deaths (13,988,011 national) and net domestic migration. 3.

**MEDSL & `tonmcg` County Presidential Returns (2016-2024):** Validates certified general-election ballots cast (154,277,745 in 2024 vs. 156,217,931 in 2020) against official state certifications including North Carolina's 5,699,141 and Mississippi's 1,228,008. 4. **OpenFEMA `DisasterDeclarationsSummaries` v2 (2020-2026):** Paginated cleanly through 19,551 federal declaration rows covering 3,238 county FIPS units to power [disaster continuity](/explore/disaster-continuity) research.

## Three Candidate Sources Deliberately Excluded

Rigorous curation depends as heavily on what stays out as what gets ingested. Three widely cited alternatives failed verification and were intentionally excluded from redistribution:

1. **Publicly Mirrored State Voter-File CSV Repos:** Excluded unconditionally under [privacy](/explore/privacy) zero-PII rules, even when distributed freely on open buckets, because shipping personal names, birth years, and residential addresses violates non-reidentification guarantees.
2. **OpenElections MS/NC 2024 Directories:** Excluded at this release because several 2024 county precinct folders remain partial PDF or OCR drafts lacking uniform five-digit FIPS county totals, whereas MEDSL and `tonmcg` certified series match official state abstracts.
3. **Authenticated `api.census.gov` Endpoints:** Rejected in favor of bulk `www2.census.gov` flat distributions so every analyst can rebuild exact tables from zero-secret scripts without registering personal API keys or risking quota throttling during automated CI builds.

## Why Sentinel Cleaning Matters Before Any Chart Renders

A subtle trap lurks inside raw 2024 EAVS spreadsheets: negative integers such as `-99` ("Data Not Available"), `-88` ("Not Applicable"), and `-77` ("Item Valid Skip") sit inside numeric columns alongside valid state totals. Any naive `SUM()` SQL query run directly on uncleaned EAVS CSVs silently corrupts regional totals. Normalizing sentinel negatives during ingestion and zero-padding California 9-digit FIPS codes before aggregation guarantees that analysts in [civic data benchmarks](/explore/civic-data-benchmarks) explore clean, audited county facts from the first SQL query onward—while pinning cryptographic digests in a manifest so every downstream browser session knows exact source bytes never drifted.

## Building Deterministic Join Pipelines Without Keys

Eliminating proprietary API tokens yields an unexpected governance benefit: county clerks, local reporters, and independent statisticians can run an identical Python extraction script on clean machines without registering vendor developer portals or inheriting commercial rate limits. When downstream users download `us_county_election_admin_cvap_2024.csv` (3,222 counties) or `fema_county_election_continuity_2020_2026.csv` (3,210 counties), each row carries exact five-digit `county_fips` join keys verified by SHA-256 digests published openly alongside upstream federal source URLs. Reproducibility stops resting on institutional authority alone and becomes straightforward file verification that anyone with a laptop can audit independently.

---
**Sources:** [OpenFEMA DisasterDeclarationsSummaries v2 Endpoint](https://www.fema.gov/api/open/v2/DisasterDeclarationsSummaries) · [MEDSL / tonmcg County Election Returns 2008-2024](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonmcg/US_County_Level_Election_Results_08-24/master/2024_US_County_Level_Presidential_Results.csv) · [U.S. Census Bureau Population Estimates CSV Directory](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2024/counties/totals/co-est2024-alldata.csv)

chunks:
Most generative analytics products repeat the same costly mistake: they ship sensitive datasets—or worse, speculative natural-language prompts—to remote foundation models that hallucinate column statistics and silently leak private tables into third-party logs. A three-tier local intelligence stack reverses that dependency by treating deterministic SQL and local full-text search as primary compute primitives inside [local-compute](/explore/local-compute) interfaces, reserving small language models strictly for optional prose transitions over verified result rows.

Foundational columnar engine design explains why browser analytical throughput no longer requires remote servers. As the DuckDB engineering specification states:

> "Vectorized query execution in WebAssembly enables relational joins, windowed aggregations, and schema introspection directly inside the client sandbox without serializing rows across network sockets."

Paired with [databases](/explore/databases) fundamentals like zero-copy File API mounts, an analyst loading a multi-million-row public record or a 3,222-county federal atlas runs instant `DESCRIBE` and aggregation passes inside Chrome or Safari worker threads. Queries that would time out serverless Edge functions finish locally without network round-trips, API rate limits, or third-party data retention agreements.

## Anatomy of the Three-Tier Execution Pipeline

A disciplined client-side intelligence system separates mathematical discovery from linguistic styling across three distinct execution bands:

1. **Tier 1: Deterministic Intent and SQL Synthesis.** Keyword and schema-aware classifiers inspect mounted column headers in real time—identifying whether `data_file` holds federal EAVS columns (`eavs_removals_total`, `cvap_2024`), MS/NC audit joins (`marigold_active_to_cvap_pct`), OpenFEMA continuity tracks (`fema_disasters_2020_2026`), or custom user CSV fields—and dispatch exact parameterized SQL statements directly into DuckDB-Wasm. Using Apache Arrow vectors converted cleanly from 64-bit `BigInt` counts into bounded JavaScript numbers, Tier 1 renders five structured dossier cards (executive headline, aggregate KPIs, sortable breakdown table, counter-context caveat, and inspectable SQL trace) at zero remote token expense. 2.

**Tier 2: Offline BM25 Research Retrieval and Small Models.** Before drafting interpretive prose, an embedded Okapi BM25 retriever queries locally bundled editorial canon and federal methodology briefs derived from sibling [systems design](/explore/systems-design) namespaces. Even on laptops disconnected from public internet inside election command tents, analysts see matching statutory rules, EAVS column renumberings, and Census sampling formulas right beside their SQL results. When WebGPU hardware or a localhost Ollama model is available, a compact 3B-class open model polishes transitional sentences strictly grounded in returned table cells rather than fabricating unverified numbers. 3.

**Tier 3: Verifiable Dossier Export.** Because every chart, KPI tile, and prose footnote cites exact SHA-256 dataset digests alongside reproducible SQL queries, a county clerk or investigative desk editor can reopen the exported HTML brief months later on an air-gapped machine and re-verify every arithmetic step independently.

## Operational Gains in Newsrooms and County Audits

Removing remote inference servers from the analytical inner loop eliminates two silent failure modes simultaneously. First, newsroom desks investigating municipal payroll exports, hospital billing CSVs, or voter-roll benchmarks no longer trigger legal hold reviews over uploading sensitive local files into SaaS AI portals. Because files mount exclusively via the browser's local `File` interface or pre-verified static `/datasets/civic/` tables, raw bytes stay pinned on local silicon. Second, response variance disappears: asking the same CVAP threshold question ten times yields identical county rankings down to the hundredth of a percent instead of probabilistic narrative drift.

## The Honest Counterargument Against Rigid SQL Templates

Skeptical product teams argue that deterministic intent routing cannot anticipate novel phrasing or subtle multi-hop analyst questions the way frontier cloud LLMs can. If a reporter asks an unanticipated comparative question across unfamiliar column aliases, brittle regex routers risk falling back to generic summaries.

That limitation is real—and easily bounded through transparent fallback telemetry. Rather than disguising a template miss behind confident prose, deterministic engines run a live schema inspection query, disclose exact matched columns alongside exact SQL executed, and expose an inspectable local SQL workbench so users can refine filters directly. Combining schema introspection with mounted primary-source knowledge corpora guarantees that when automated inference stops, verifiable primary measurement takes over cleanly. In civic and financial reporting inside [local-first](/explore/local-first) tools, predictable accuracy beats improvised eloquence on every single query.

---
**Sources:** [DuckDB-Wasm Architectural Overview](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/wasm/overview) · [Apache Arrow Columnar Format Spec](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html) · [Okapi BM25 Probabilistic Retrieval (Robertson & Zaragoza)](https://www.staff.city.ac.uk/~sbrp622/papers/foundations_bm25_review.pdf)

Raw registration counts routinely mislead state observers when separated from underlying demographic churn. Comparing North Carolina's centralized 100-county voter file against Mississippi's 82-county roll looks baffling at first glance if one inspects raw active-voter percentages alone. Only when joined county by county with 2020-2024 Census Citizen Voting Age Population (CVAP) estimates, 90% confidence intervals, and domestic migration series does the administrative story snap into clear focus.

Statisticians who publish small-area Census estimates caution repeatedly against ignoring confidence bounds when calculating administrative ratios. As the Census Bureau's ACS CVAP documentation explains:

> "Estimates derived from the 5-year American Community Survey reflect multi-year sample averages and carry explicit 90 percent margins of error that widen sharply in rural counties with smaller populations."

Evaluating state voter rolls inside [civic data benchmarks](/explore/civic-data-benchmarks) demands applying that statistical discipline before sounding alarms. Across North Carolina's 100 counties, 2026 registration rolls total 7,900,954 voters—including 6,902,431 active and nearly one million inactive records—set against 7,898,142 estimated citizen adults and 5,699,141 certified 2024 presidential ballots. Exactly one North Carolina county exceeds its upper 90% CVAP confidence bound on active voters: coastal Brunswick County, posting 136,822 active voters against 128,976 ± 410 CVAP (106.08%), a surge directly illuminated by +33,821 net domestic in-migrants recorded between 2020 and 2024 while ACS 5-year averages lag recent retirees moving in.

## The Maintenance Velocity Contrast: 971,554 Removals vs. 148,200

Zooming into federal list-maintenance fields exposes the sharper operational divergence between the two states. Under [election integrity](/explore/election-integrity) standards anchored in NVRA Section 8, active cleanups require mailing statutory confirmation notices (`A10a`) across federal cycles before purging stale records (`A12a`): 1. **North Carolina's High-Throughput Maintenance:** In 2024 EAVS V2.0, North Carolina reported 707,618 confirmation notices sent and 971,554 removals completed—led by Mecklenburg County (122,082 removals, 88,480 notices, and 31,883 recorded deaths from 2020-2024), Wake County (104,164 removals and 56,879 notices), and Guilford County (50,218 removals).

Centralized state board coordination keeps confirmation cycles running evenly across urban metros and rural counties alike, holding inactive queues visible until statutory waiting windows expire. 2. **Mississippi's Rural Out-Migration Drag:** Across 82 counties holding 1,882,342 active voters (2,112,449 total registered against 2,221,778 CVAP and 1,228,008 certified 2024 presidential votes), Mississippi logged 100,185 confirmation notices and 148,200 removals. Seven counties exceed their upper 90% CVAP bound even after confidence bounds: Humphreys (116.01%, 6,404 active vs. 5,520 ± 23 CVAP), Tallahatchie (103.94%), Smith (101.93%), Yazoo (101.88%, despite -3,507 net domestic out-migration), Hancock (101.81%, +1,114 migration), Holmes (101.25%), and Hinds (100.25%, 165,189 active vs. 164,779 ± 368 CVAP alongside -17,670 net domestic out-migration).

## How Disaster Resilience Intersected North Carolina's Cycle

Comparing both states side by side also spotlights operational continuity under stress. Thirty-nine western North Carolina counties received federal `DR-4827-NC` declarations during Hurricane Helene less than six weeks before November 2024, yet certified turnout across those declared jurisdictions grew from 2,338,633 in 2020 to 2,396,685 in 2024. Robust statewide early voting and temporary emergency polling relocations kept voter access intact while centralized registration systems reconciled provisional and displaced absentee packets cleanly.

## Testing the Honest Counterargument on List Cleanliness

Election administrators in net out-migration rural counties correctly note that federal law forbids immediate removal simply because a resident moves out of county or skips two elections. Under federal Section 8 waiting periods, an out-migrant placed on inactive or active-pending confirmation queues legitimately remains counted across two consecutive federal general elections before statutory cancellation—producing apparent roll inflation in shrinking Delta counties that does not reflect fraud or improper voting.

Paired applied [mathematics](/explore/mathematics) settles both points constructively. When county audits combine active-to-CVAP exceedance flags with domestic migration trajectories and EAVS confirmation notice volumes, analysts distinguish rapid-growth lag (Brunswick County, NC) from stalled mailing queues in declining-population counties (Hinds and Humphreys, MS), routing limited county clerk budgets to physical confirmation outreach rather than partisan rhetoric.

---
**Sources:** [U.S. Census County Population Estimates 2020-2024](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest/datasets/2020-2024/counties/totals/co-est2024-alldata.csv) · [U.S. EAC 2024 EAVS V2.0 CSV Release](https://www.eac.gov/sites/default/files/2026-02/2024_EAVS_for_Public_Release_nolabel_V2_csv.zip) · [MEDSL 2024 Official State Presidential Returns](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MEDSL/2024-elections-official/main/2024-president-state.csv)
